**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 10, 2026**
**Member:** Rowan Carter | **Member ID:** W473677710
**Reference number:** POC-CD6AF51965-72160
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare, Commercial/ACA, South Carolina
**Governing policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy — https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), denied on August 10, 2026 under reference number POC-CD6AF51965-72160. I am asking Molina to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. The reason given in the notice is that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I respectfully disagree, and I believe the records already in Molina's possession show otherwise when they are measured against Molina's own published policy.

My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval, submitted this request along with the supporting records and has documented that this surgery is needed.

## What the plan's own policy says, and what my records show

Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy sets out the criteria for arthroscopic shoulder procedures. Its criteria sets begin with language such as:

> "Diagnostic arthroscopy may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

**1. Severe, disabling pain and/or documented loss of function.** The policy requires:

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records establish this. I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. On examination, my provocative testing was positive on the affected side and my range of motion was limited by pain. The MRI performed on July 6, 2026 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.

**2. Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months.** This is the criterion the denial turns on. The policy states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records establish this as well. My non-surgical treatment has been continuous and well documented, and it spans far more than three months:

- **NSAIDs for 8 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **A corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026**, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy from May 23, 2026 through July 18, 2026 — 24 completed visits over 8 weeks**, focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, my non-surgical management ran from the start of NSAID therapy through my discharge from physical therapy in July 2026 — a continuous course well longer than three months — and it involved three distinct treatments rather than one. Every one of them failed to give me lasting relief.

The excerpt above ends in a colon and introduces a list of accepted conservative measures that I was not given a copy of. The policy also contains additional criteria sets for other arthroscopic procedures — including debridement, loose body removal, synovectomy, labral repair/biceps tenodesis, distal clavicle excision and subacromial decompression/acromioplasty, capsulorrhaphy, and capsular release — each of which begins with its own "ALL of the following criteria" language and lists conditions that are not reproduced in the portion of the policy available to me. I am therefore unable to address any criterion beyond the two quoted above, and I ask that the reviewer apply the policy's full text to the records already submitted.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

Molina holds the criteria that were used to deny my request; I do not. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination**, together with the specific criterion Molina found unmet and the credentials of the reviewer who made the decision. Please send these to me at the address above so that I can respond to the actual standard that was used.

## What I am asking for

Please overturn the denial dated August 10, 2026 (reference POC-CD6AF51965-72160) and authorize rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. If any part of my file is missing or if additional documentation would help, please tell me exactly what is needed and I will ask my surgeon's office to send it promptly rather than have the request denied a second time on the same ground.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 6, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that window. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for my plan. I understand I may also use the member portal at molinahealthcare.com or call the Member Services number on my ID card, and I ask that Molina confirm receipt of this appeal in writing.

Thank you for taking the time to review my case and the records my surgeon submitted.

Sincerely,

__________________________
Rowan Carter
Member ID: W473677710
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
Phone: [Phone number]
Email: [Email address]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-10; physical therapy discharge note; MRI report dated 2026-07-06; medication and injection records; surgeon's office notes]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
